q-er-02.Acceptable if the receptacle tests GFCI: Ask what GFCI protection actually does. Does it keep rain from getting into the box?
q-er-02.Cosmetic damage to the cover, which the: Ask what that cover is for. Is its job about looks, or about keeping something out?
q-er-02.Shock hazard; turn off the circuit and r: Ask where the utility's equipment ends. Does it repair wiring devices on the house side of the meter?

q-er-08.Do not report it, because a 1987 house i: Ask whether NC ties what you report to the year a house was built, or to what you find.
q-er-08.Acceptable, because the receptacle's pol: Ask whether correct polarity protects a person at a wet sink from a ground fault.
q-er-08.Cite a code violation and require the se: Ask whether a home inspection checks code compliance, and whether the inspector decides what a seller must fix.

q-er-10.Acceptable, as long as the tape is intac: Ask whether intact tape does anything to contain heat or sparks if that splice ever fails.
q-er-10.Acceptable in attics, since they are uno: Ask whether a failing splice needs a person nearby to start a fire in insulation and framing.
q-er-10.Fire hazard; recommend rewiring the atti: Ask how many problems the stem actually shows. Does one splice tell you about every circuit up there?

q-ap-06.Acceptable if the run is short and the d: Ask whether a short, straight run changes what the duct is made of, or how that material handles heat.
q-ap-06.Acceptable as long as the lint filter is: Ask whether the lint filter catches everything, or whether some lint still reaches the duct.
q-ap-06.Fire hazard; refer to the fire marshal b: Ask whether a fire marshal inspects appliance venting in a private home, and whether that referral fits a house sale.

q-ap-09.Acceptable while it is not leaking; note: Ask what a bulge says about the hose's inner strength. Does no leak today mean it will hold?
q-ap-09.Not reportable, because a washer is not: Ask whether not having to inspect the washer stops you from reporting a hazard you can already see.
q-ap-09.Shut off the main water valve until a pl: Ask whether the bulge is in the building's supply piping, or in the hose that links the washer to it.

q-eh-07.Acceptable; exterior entry steps are exe: Ask whether a fall down entry steps is any less serious because the steps are outdoors.
q-eh-07.Acceptable; a handrail is required start: Ask whether 6 is the riser count you studied for handrails, or a number borrowed from a different rule for steps.
q-eh-07.Structural defect; refer to a structural: Ask whether the stem says the steps are cracked, moving, or failing to carry weight.

q-hv-03.Acceptable; 2 in is the standard clearan: Ask whether you are thinking of a double-wall vent. Does a pipe with only one metal layer run cooler or hotter?
q-hv-03.Acceptable as long as the joist shows no: Ask whether clearance rules are written around visible damage, or around what years of heat do to wood.
q-hv-03.Fire hazard; have the fire department in: Ask whether a fire department inspects private homes for a sale, and who actually works on furnace venting.

q-hv-11.Acceptable, because the vented attic wil: Ask whether attic vents are meant to handle a duct's full airflow, cold and damp, all season long.
q-hv-11.Major defect; replace the attic duct sys: Ask how much of the duct system the stem describes. Does one loose joint condemn every run?
q-hv-11.Not reportable, since attic ductwork is: Ask whether NC treats ducts in the attic differently from ducts anywhere else in the house.

q-ai-03.Acceptable, because the attic itself is: Ask whether attic vents can clear a shower's worth of moist air before it reaches cold sheathing.
q-ai-03.Refer to a structural engineer for moist: Ask whether the stem describes damage to the roof framing, and what a structural engineer would assess here.
q-ai-03.Not reportable; exhaust fans are not in: Ask whether NC lists bathroom venting among the systems you are required to inspect.

q-ai-07.Acceptable if the ladder holds your full: Ask whether one test load today tells you how brittle screws behave after years of use.
q-ai-07.Refer to a structural engineer to evalua: Ask what in the stem points at the ceiling framing. Is a structural engineer the trade for ladder hardware?
q-ai-07.Not reportable, because attic stairs are: Ask whether the SOP exclusions you studied actually name attic stairs, or a ladder you can see and use.

q-dk-04.Acceptable if most of the holes are fill: Ask whether a hanger's rated strength assumes that some of its holes are left empty.
q-dk-04.Acceptable, because screws are stronger: Ask whether stronger in one direction means stronger in shear, which is how a hanger is loaded.
q-dk-04.Imminent collapse; tear down the deck an: Ask whether the stem describes broken or rotted framing. Does tearing down the deck match what you see?

q-dk-09.Acceptable, because ground-contact treat: Ask whether treated wood is rot-proof or only rot-resistant. What did the probe just tell you?
q-dk-09.Condemn the deck; recommend demolishing: Ask how much of the deck the stem says has failed. Does one soft post decide the whole structure?
q-dk-09.Not reportable, since probing is an inva: Ask whether NC requires probing where you suspect deterioration, even in a visual inspection.

q-fd-05.Acceptable; stacked shims are a normal w: Ask whether shims being allowed means that loose, crushed shims are allowed too.
q-fd-05.Foundation failure; refer for underpinni: Ask whether anything in the stem says the pier or its footing has sunk or cracked.
q-fd-05.Not reportable without first calculating: Ask whether reporting a support problem you can see requires any calculation under NC rules.

q-eg-04.Acceptable, since the bars improve the b: Ask whether security is the only job a bedroom window has under the rules you studied.
q-eg-04.Refer to the fire marshal to condemn the: Ask whether a fire marshal inspects private homes for a sale, and whether closing off a room is your call.
q-eg-04.Acceptable if the bedroom door leads to: Ask whether the escape rule counts exits through the door, or treats the window on its own.

q-pl-05.Sewage hazard; refer to the health depar: Ask what a county health department oversees, and whether one joint in a private drain line is theirs.
q-pl-05.Not reportable, because the crawlspace i: Ask whether NC excludes the crawlspace, or asks you to inspect the plumbing you can reach and see there.
q-pl-05.Monitor it and re-check at the final wal: Ask whether an active drip you can see today is something to wait on, and who attends a final walkthrough.

q-ra-02.They mean the roof has failed and needs: Ask whether the stem describes a roof-wide failure or several nails. Does that add up to a new roof?
q-ra-02.They matter in hurricane zones, not in n: Ask whether the concern with an exposed nail head depends on wind at all.
q-ra-02.Exposed nails are normal along the ridge: Ask what covers the nails at ridge and hip caps on a correct install. Should heads show anywhere?
